question.text: Will the Save Our Bacon Act be enacted into law before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2027, federal legislation is enacted into law that preempts state regulation of out-of-state pork production.

Specifically, the enacted text must establish that pork producers may raise and market their products in interstate commerce, free from state or local production-process standards imposed on pigs physically raised outside the state's borders. The statute may also cover other livestock (e.g., cattle, veal, dairy), but pork coverage is what this question turns on.
question.fine_print:
* Enactment may occur via presidential signature, becoming law without signature, or veto override. The legislation may be a standalone bill or a provision within other legislation such as the Farm Bill, appropriations, or the NDAA.
* Court rulings, executive orders, or USDA rulemakings achieving similar effects do not count.
* A bill that grandfathers existing state laws, applies only prospectively to laws enacted after a certain date, or contains a state opt-out provision will not resolve **Yes**.
* The effective date of the bill does not matter, as long as it is enacted before July 1, 2027.

research:
I found no sign that Save Our Bacon language has been enacted, and nothing that settles the question yet. As of 2026-11-19 it exists only in the House-passed farm bill. The Senate committee version leaves it out, and Democrats take both chambers on 2027-01-03.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-19: Congress.gov pages for H.R. 7567 and H.R. 4673 returned 403 (blocked by a bot check), so I could not read the official actions list directly. Every news source I found agrees the latest action on H.R. 7567 is House passage on 2026-04-30, with no Senate passage. [congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/7567)
- I found no record of H.R. 4673 moving on its own past introduction (2025-07-23). [Hinson release](https://hinson.house.gov/media/press-releases/hinson-introduces-save-our-bacon-act-block-californias-radical-prop-12-protect)
- The question resolves on whether a law is enacted; there is no data series behind it.

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. No farm bill or other vehicle containing the preemption language has passed the Senate.
- The farm bill extension in P.L. 119-37 (November 2025) expired at the end of FY2026, and I found no new extension. [CRS IF12047 summary via search](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF12047)
- Grandfather risk: the Ernst amendment offered in the Senate committee reportedly would *preserve* Prop 12 and other existing state laws and block only future state mandates. The fine print says a version like that would **not** resolve Yes. [KTVO](https://www.ktvo.com/news/local/senate-agriculture-committee-advances-farm-bill-as-prop-12-debate-moves-to-senate-floor/article_7fa63fb4-8d41-479d-a345-44739e3bd8ee.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-18: The House left early for Thanksgiving with government funding unresolved past the December 11 continuing-resolution deadline. [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2026/11/18/house-gop-skipping-town-early-weeks-left-in-majority)
- 2026-11-16: Iowa Senator-elect Zach Turek (D) said "I'm not sure we're going to see a farm bill pass." Boozman's office says talks continue. The main Democratic sticking point is SNAP cost-sharing, and an unfinished bill starts over in the new Congress. [DTN](https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/news/world-policy/article/2026/11/16/iowa-sen-elect-turek-wants-farm-bill)
- 2026-11-16: The National Council of Farmer Cooperatives urged leaders to pass a five-year farm bill in the lame duck. [Oklahoma Farm Report](https://www.oklahomafarmreport.com/2026/11/16/farmer-cooperatives-urge-congress-to-finish-the-farm-bill-during-lame-duck-session/)
- Mid-November 2026: Agri-Pulse reports Boozman offered a one-year SNAP cost-share delay as his "final offer," while Klobuchar wants two years. Without a SNAP deal the bill is unlikely to move. Klobuchar is the Minnesota governor-elect, and Bennet is the likely next Senate Ag chair. [Agri-Pulse](https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/25480-thune-seeks-pathway-for-farm-bill-amid-lame-duck-squeeze), [Agri-Pulse week ahead](https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/25476-washington-week-ahead-farm-bill-faces-lame-duck-challenge)
- 2026-11-06: Boozman said he is willing to compromise and warned of "at least a one-year delay" otherwise. He named Prop 12 as one of the open issues. Adjournment is scheduled for December 18. [Brownfield](https://brownfieldagnews.com/news/boozman-farm-bill-compromise-possible-during-lame-duck-session/)
- 2026-11-03/04: Democrats won both chambers, with about 54 Senate seats and 228+ House seats in early counts. Iowa's Senate seat flipped. [OPB/NPR](https://www.opb.org/article/2026/11/04/2026-midterms-democrats-win-the-senate/)
- 2026-10-16: Boozman and House Ag Chair Thompson both said they were optimistic that the provision "or something similar" would be in a final package. [humaneaction.org news](https://humaneaction.org/protect-state-laws/news)
- Fall 2026: the American Meat Producers PAC reportedly ran a $3 million campaign against supporters of Save Our Bacon. (Source: search-result summary only, not checked.)
- 2026-09-16: The Senate Agriculture Committee advanced Boozman's bill 12-11 on party lines, with no Prop 12 language. Boozman refused to take up the Ernst amendment. The bill needs 60 votes on the floor. [KTVO](https://www.ktvo.com/news/local/senate-agriculture-committee-advances-farm-bill-as-prop-12-debate-moves-to-senate-floor/article_7fa63fb4-8d41-479d-a345-44739e3bd8ee.html), [DTN](https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/columns/washington-insider/article/2026/09/17/senate-farm-bill-reported-committee)
- June 2026: Boozman's discussion draft also left out a Prop 12 fix. [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/livestock-management/senate-farm-bill-draft-omits-prop-12-fix-for-pork-industry), [Hyde-Smith](https://www.hydesmith.senate.gov/boozman-releases-farm-bill-20-text-built-bipartisan-path-without-prop-12-e15)

## 4. Base rates
- The King Amendment was in the House farm bills of 2013-14 and 2018 and was dropped in conference both times. The EATS Act (2021, 2023) and Save Our Bacon never became law. Enactments to date: zero. [AWI](https://awionline.org/awi-quarterly/2013-fall/king-amendment%E2%80%99s-attack-state-animal-welfare-laws)
- Farm bills routinely slip: the 2018 bill has been extended three times. [CRS](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF12047)
- Lame-duck sessions right after a party loses Congress rarely produce a full farm bill. Analysts say Democrats now have less reason to accept a deal they could renegotiate from a stronger position in January. [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/farm-policy-news/a-blue-wave-a-lame-duck-and-a-farm-bill-short-on-runway)
- After January 3, 2027, a Democratic House and Senate would have to pass the language. The Senate committee had already left it out under Republican control.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket "SAVE Act" markets supplied with this request match the question. They are about the SAVE / SAVE America voter-citizenship bill (about 1-4%).
- Kalshi "reconciliation bill becomes law before Jul 1, 2027": 14%. This is only loosely related; Prop 12 preemption would probably not survive the Senate's Byrd rule, which limits reconciliation bills to budget-related provisions.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on Save Our Bacon, the EATS Act or the 2026 farm bill.

## 6. Upcoming events
- 2026-11 to 12-18: the lame duck (scheduled adjournment December 18). Watch for a negotiated Senate floor vote on the farm bill or a combined House-Senate final bill, and whether Prop 12 language is included and in what form (full preemption or grandfathered).
- 2026-12-11: the government funding deadline. An omnibus or continuing resolution could carry farm bill items, including an extension.
- 2027-01-03: the 120th Congress convenes under Democratic control and the farm bill process starts over. Ag committee leadership changes: likely Bennet as Senate Ag chair, and Thompson needs a waiver to stay top Republican on House Ag.
- Through 2027-06-30: possible farm bill extension or FY2027 appropriations bills. I found no reporting that Democratic leaders plan to include the preemption language.

- Pattern: the House includes the language and the Senate (60-vote threshold) refuses it. That is the same split now, and from January a Democratic House and Senate will control committees and floor time.

The opposing advocates expect the pork lobby to try again. [Humane World](https://www.humaneworld.org/en/blog/midterm-elections-big-pork-prop-12)

- Watch whether any deal grandfathers existing state laws or applies only to future ones. Under the fine print, that version would resolve No.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 7 months remain until July 1, 2027, but the practical window is the lame-duck session, which adjourns December 18, 2026. For Yes, Congress must enact a law, whether a farm bill, omnibus, or rider, that fully preempts state production-process standards on pork raised out of state. The law must have no grandfathering of existing laws like Prop 12, no prospective-only limit, and no state opt-out.

(b) If nothing changes, the language stays only in the House-passed H.R. 7567. The Senate bill omits it, and the 119th Congress ends without it. The outcome is No.

(c) The reference class is the King Amendment, the EATS Act and Save Our Bacon across the 2013-14, 2018, 2021-24 and 2025-26 cycles. The House has included the language several times, and it has been enacted zero times out of roughly 4-5 tries, with the Senate or conference dropping it each time. A rough base rate is under 10% per cycle, even with a Republican trifecta.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The House passed the farm bill with the language on April 30, 2026.
- On October 16, 2026, Boozman and Thompson said they were optimistic that the provision "or something similar" would be in a final package.
- Ernst insisted on a fix on November 17.
- On November 5, analysts said all titles except nutrition were agreed, and a deal could ride an omnibus.

Evidence for No:
- The Senate committee bill left the language out, and Boozman refused the Ernst amendment on September 16.
- Democrats won both chambers on November 3.
- On November 17, Bennet, the likely next Senate Ag chair, said Prop 12 language was left out "for a reason."
- The NPPC CEO reportedly conceded after the midterms that a farm bill was unlikely this Congress.
- The SNAP standoff is unresolved, and the House left early on November 18.
- Even a compromise is likely to look like Ernst's grandfathered version, which would resolve No.
- From January 2027, Democrats control both chambers.

(e) No scenario: the SNAP talks fail and Congress passes a CR or omnibus with a farm bill extension and no Prop 12 language. The 120th Congress under Democrats does not revive the language. Yes scenario: a last-minute deal pairs a two-year SNAP delay with Republican wins, and full Prop 12 preemption is attached to a must-pass omnibus. Enough Senate Democrats accept it to reach 60 votes, and the President signs in December.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 5-8% per cycle. I move down for three reasons:
- Senate exclusion even under Republican control.
- The Democratic wave, which removes most of the window after January 3.
- The extra grandfathering hurdle, since the likeliest compromise form would not count.

My estimate is about 15% for a lame-duck farm bill, times about 15% that it carries full non-grandfathered preemption. That gives about 2%, plus a small chance from other vehicles. The closest market is the narrower Manifold question at 2.8%, which is consistent with this.

Probability: 3%

(a) About 7.5 months remain until July 1, 2027, and the realistic window is much shorter. For Yes, Congress must enact a law, most likely a final farm bill or an omnibus rider, that preempts state production-process standards on pork raised out of state. The preemption must apply to existing laws like Prop 12, with no grandfathering, no prospective-only limit and no state opt-out. The practical window is the lame duck, with adjournment planned for December 18, 2026. After January 3, Democrats control both chambers.

(b) Status quo: no enactment. The language exists only in the House-passed H.R. 7567. The Senate committee bill excludes it, and no conference report exists. The status quo resolves No.

(c) Base rate: King Amendment and EATS-style preemption has been in House farm bills in the 2013-14 and 2018 cycles and was dropped in conference each time. It has been enacted 0 of roughly 4 times. A lame-duck farm bill passing at all after a party loses Congress is also uncommon. Combining these gives a base rate of about 2-5%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - On April 30, 2026, the House passed the bill with the language.
  - On October 16, 2026, Boozman and Thompson said they were optimistic that the provision "or something similar" would be in a final package.
  - Boozman said Prop 12 would be resolved in conference.
  - On November 5, 2026, analysts reported that all titles except nutrition are agreed, and an omnibus vehicle is possible.
- For No:
  - On September 16, 2026, the Senate committee passed its bill on party lines without Prop 12 language and blocked the Ernst amendment. That amendment would have grandfathered existing laws, which would resolve No anyway.
  - The Democratic midterm sweep on November 3-4 gives Democrats reason to wait until January.

(e)
- No scenario: the SNAP talks fail and Congress passes a CR with a farm bill extension by December 18. The Democratic 120th Congress then shows no interest in Prop 12 preemption before July 2027.
- Yes scenario: a SNAP compromise is reached in December, and Republicans insist on Prop 12 language as the price. Democrats accept full preemption in a farm bill attached to the omnibus, and the President signs it before January 3.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 3%. The House passage and leadership optimism argue slightly upward. Several things argue downward: the Senate's exclusion, the likelihood that any compromise is grandfathered rather than full preemption, Democratic leverage after the election, and the short lame duck. These roughly offset. A Democratic Congress in 2027 adds almost nothing. I stay near the Manifold anchor, adjusting a little for this question's broader vehicle coverage.

(f) I start at roughly 3% from the base rate. The lame duck is the only realistic window, and even if a farm bill passes, full preemption without grandfathering is unlikely given the Senate's stance and Democratic leverage.
